segments.description: Welcome coaches to the Grand Slam Coaches Conference and thank you for tuning in to day three of our locker room question and answer sessions. I think it's a really cool way to understand where you've come from and where you want to go. And then of course, where you are today. So, nah, cool. And let's start with that one. You pose a fairly deep question early in your presentation. Which was, what are you born to do? So how does one go about starting to answer that one? Well, the first thing I would say about that, one of the coaching models that I use

with a lot of my mentees, and I'm also involved with the Tennis Australia Coach Connects mentee program, is something I called the onion model. So if you think about an onion, and it's the center of that onion, you have sort of, it looks like a piece symbol. You've sort of got three inner core, what I call superpowers. And then you've got all these extra layers, or as Shrek would say, I guess, that ogres have lots and lots of layers. We as humans are very, very complex. In fact, that's one of the most things I find fascinating about coaching, is how do you unpack the layers to get to the core of understanding the player-centered approach that we, of course, heard Stephen Hust talk so beautifully about and eloquently about. And I think that those three things that you can come up with about who you are, no matter what stage in your journey you're at, is exactly where you're meant to be at that stage in your journey. So my sort of three inner core superpowers now, after coaching for sort of many years, were a lot different to when I first started. And I think it's a matter of unpacking that through looking at, of course, some of your early passions. So what are you passionate about? Because it's amazing the correlation between what you're passionate about actually relates to what you're really good at. So I think that's a really great place to start and note that it changes over the years. And eventually you'll find that it will land somewhere. And maybe that might be just for a time period. What do you think, Brett? Oh, I just love the language. You're very deliberate in the use of your language, I know. And I love this concept of finding your inner superpowers. So I think it's the people that you surround yourself with, it's who you're influenced by.
